paragraphs: Ealing Council runs its own fostering service, Ealing Fostering Connections, for children in the borough's care, and the services listed above also cover Ealing. New enquiries to the council now go through Foster with West London, the regional recruitment hub that brings eight west London councils together, so you can ask about Ealing and its neighbours in one conversation.

In its most recent recruitment drive the council said it was looking in particular for carers for sibling groups of all ages, school-age children including teenagers, babies, parents with their babies, and children with additional needs and disabilities. A councillor quoted when the offer was improved described the shortage of carers as a national problem that is especially sharp in Ealing.

In October 2024 the council's cabinet agreed an 18.5% rise in fees and allowances. Its 2025 package for its own carers adds full council tax exemption for eligible carers living in Ealing (with reimbursement for those living outside the borough), free parking in residents' bays across the borough, free garden waste collection, discounts at council leisure centres, therapeutic support from the council's clinical psychologists, an out-of-hours support team, peer support and the Mockingbird scheme, where a group of fostering households supports one another around an experienced hub carer.

Information sessions, in person and online, run through the year. Talk to the council and to two or three of the services above, compare the training and support each offers, and look at the London page too if you live near the borough's edge.
